question.text: What will happen when a block of copper metal is dropped into a beaker containing a solution of <math> <mrow> <mn>1</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext>M</mtext></mrow> </math> <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math>?

options.text: The copper metal will dissolve with evolution of oxygen gas.
The copper metal will dissolve with evolution of hydrogen gas.
The copper metal will dissolve and zinc metal will be deposited.

solution.text:
Zn is above Cu in electrochemical series. So, Zn will reduce Cu2+ to Cu.
Cu + Zn2+ → No reaction
Displacement reaction is feasible in opposite direction only.
Cu2+ + Zn  → Zn2+ + Cu ↓
